A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, models and central results. The complete main text and appendices are readable, and relocated proofs and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original neural-network experiments on Gaussian-mixture data, including training-point and test-point margin statistics in Figures 1–3.

after.justification: V3 reports revised Gaussian experiments and original MNIST, training-progress and network-width experiments in Figures 1–5.

M1.justification: The core attacks remain. Appendix G adds Algorithm 2, a restricted reconstruction variant retaining only Algorithm 1's non-flat-interval branch. Section 5 also proposes interval-valued reconstruction outputs under parameter perturbations. These are limited extensions of the existing procedures.

E1.justification: V2's empirical coverage is confined to synthetic Gaussian-mixture data. V3 retains that coverage and adds training and membership-inference evaluation on MNIST images in Appendix E.1, substantially extending the represented data domain.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluations against competing privacy attacks. Carlini, Zarifzadeh and Golbari are newly discussed in v3 but are not evaluated comparators; the fully connected and convolutional networks are attacked architectures.

E3.justification: V3 introduces MNIST resolution sweeps using bicubic resizing and 4,000 training epochs, including a convolutional architecture. It also adds per-epoch Gaussian evaluation at dimension 500 and hidden-width sweeps. The original Gaussian experiment's stated 10,000-neuron architecture and 20/5,000 training/test sample counts remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's dimension sensitivity experiment, Appendix E.2 tests behavior throughout training, using epochs as a proxy for proximity to KKT convergence. Appendix E.3 tests dependence on network width. These add substantial evidence about convergence sensitivity and architectural robustness.

E5.justification: The main Gaussian results change from averaging 50 instantiations in v2 to 10 independent runs in v3. V3 also introduces shaded bands around plotted means, although their statistical meaning is not defined. This changes reporting without establishing additional runs or formal significance testing.

E6.justification: The Gaussian curves in v2 Figures 1–3 are replaced by numerically different curves in v3 Figure 1. Figures 2–5 add MNIST outcomes, declining test-point exceedance during training and approximately width-independent behavior. V3 also newly reports 100% training accuracy and at least 85% test accuracy for the main experiments.

T1.justification: Section 5 adds Lipschitz perturbation bounds and reconstruction stability arguments requiring nondegenerate weights and slopes. Appendix G adds Theorem G.1 and a proof for the restricted reconstruction procedure without local-optimality and always-active-neuron assumptions. Additionally, v2 Lemma A.1 becomes Lemma F.1 with an open rather than closed interval; most existing proofs are retained.

C1.justification: V3's contribution statement explicitly includes the local-optimality and always-active-neuron requirements for reconstruction, which v2 stated only in the detailed theorem. The abstract also explicitly qualifies the high-dimensional guarantee by near-orthogonality. The central attacks and priority claim remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds specific limitations concerning deeper networks, higher-dimensional reconstruction and the role of separation versus near-orthogonality. It also discusses estimating margins with reference models, expands the explanation of balanced KKT weights, and clarifies that moderate-dimensional experiments explore behavior outside the guaranteed regime.

D1.justification: Appendix E supplies new implementation information, including CNN channel counts of 32 and 64, bicubic image resizing, a 4,000-epoch budget and per-epoch evaluation. The code repository link is unchanged. MNIST sample counts and class selection remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V3 substantially revises positioning around Golbari et al.'s empirical implicit-bias membership attack and Refael et al.'s reconstruction limitations, distinguishing these from sufficient conditions for provable attacks. It also adds Carlini and Zarifzadeh connections and revises the differential-privacy discussion and citations.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction and related work, places membership inference before reconstruction, and incorporates the former standalone experiment section into Section 3.2. It separates shared notation into Appendix A, moves univariate proofs to Appendix F, and adds summary, limitations and broader-impact sections.

P2.justification: The original three empirical plots become a paired Figure 1, without the separate low-dimensional zoom. V3 adds four paired experimental figures and another algorithm display; the original proof illustration is retained as Figure 6. The document template, author block, headings and algorithm formatting also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V3 states the reconstruction assumptions more accurately and adds useful convergence, width and MNIST checks, alongside perturbation analysis and clearer limitations. These improve scope clarity and empirical support. The gain is limited by unspecified MNIST sampling details, undefined shaded bands, and retained text claiming 80% below-margin test points at d = 20 that conflicts with revised Figure 1b. Algorithm 2 also contains a breakpoint-index typo, using w_1 instead of w_i.
